name: Karin Karlsbro - Projet de décision du Conseil
title: RECOMMENDATION on the draft Council decision on the termination of the Voluntary Partnership Agreement between the European Union and the Republic of Cameroon on forest law enforcement, governance and trade in timber and derived products to the Union
part_text:
The European Parliament agrees to end a 2011 deal with Cameroon on timber trade. The deal was meant to make sure wood sold to the EU was legally sourced. Cameroon did not set up the promised checks and tracking systems, and most of its timber now goes to Asia. Ending the deal means EU cooperation with Cameroon on forests should focus on preparing the country for the EU's upcoming rules against deforestation.

- The EU–Cameroon timber partnership ends; no new legal checks or tracking systems are set up.
- It affects Cameroon's timber trade with the EU and EU efforts to keep illegal wood out.
- Next, EU support to Cameroon shifts toward meeting the EU's deforestation rules.
